//: The measured cell, the pinned font, the toolchain, and where the design disagrees with the product. Each contradiction is a bug in docs/design/ or a decision the developer made against it, not a bug in the app; it leaves when the design is fixed upstream or the decision reversed. See crates/review/src/baseline.rs.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `A launch` draws the mark as 18 × 6 cells of `1ch` × `--row` (24px) on a 14px font — an 8.4 × 12px half-cell, so the letter is about as wide as it is tall.
contradictions.design_also_says: A terminal's row is shorter: on the cell `measure` pins (8 × 18) the half-cell is 8 × 9, and the same 18 × 6 cells draw the A a quarter shorter than the frame does, and a third again as wide as it is tall.
contradictions.app_follows: The frame's letter redrawn 7 rows tall on its own 18 columns by the generator (`fit_to_terminal` in `crates/review/src/tokens.rs`): the frame's stroke, its outer edge sampled along 14 half-rows, each half-row the fill of the frame's nearest. At 6 rows the rule gives the frame's cells exactly. The launch card is one row taller. 7 rows, not the 8 that would keep the letter's own proportion, because the frame's facts sit on 24px rows too: at 8 the mark outweighs them, at 7 the letter is a little wide and the balance close to the frame's. Only the mark is redrawn. Retired when the design draws the mark for a terminal's cell.

contradictions.design_says: The glyph table (guidelines/glyphs.html, README's Iconography) contains no box-drawing characters, and nothing inside a window is stroked.
contradictions.design_also_says: The design system has no table component at all — its components are Frame, Field, StatusBar, ContextBar, UserEcho, Prose, Disclosure, PlanStep, Mark, LaunchCard, QuestionPanel, CommandRow and the review set — and a set of flat grounds cannot express a two-dimensional grid of cell boundaries.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0002 — a markdown table in assistant prose is drawn with `┌ ┬ ┐ ├ ┼ ┤ └ ┴ ┘ ─ │`, scoped to that one construct. Retired when the design system gains a table component.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `F commands` types `/` and lists `clear` and `exit`, with no shortcut column; the design system's `CommandRow` still shows `changes`, `undo` (`↺`) and `quit` (`⌃D`), a key right-flush like a menu.
contradictions.design_also_says: Nothing in the design names `/resume` (ADR 0005, a shipped feature), `/model`, `/connect` (ADR 0012), `/theme`, `/reload` (ADR 0017), `/update` or `/help`, and the product has neither `/changes` nor `/undo`.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's decisions of 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-25: `/resume`, `/model`, `/connect` (ADR 0012, 2026-09-26), `/quit` and `/exit` (one command, both in the list), `/clear`, `/theme`, `/reload` (ADR 0017), `/update` and `/help` — every command the product answers, none left out (the developer's call, 2026-09-29) — with no shortcut column — as frame F now draws it. The panel's grid, tones, completion and selection are the frame's exactly; only its rows differ. `/changes` and `/undo` will not be built (the developer, 2026-09-27).

contradictions.design_says: `tokens/layout.css` is the grid, and the app draws every measure through it: `--margin-x`, `--body-x`, `--number-col` and the rest, each a token the frames read with `var(--…)`.
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame E's `QuestionPanel` positions its contents with measures no token names: the panel's text is `padding:0 3ch` inside it, and each option row is `margin:0 1ch` inside the panel.
contradictions.app_follows: Frame E's values, as the named constants `PANEL_PAD` (3) and `OPTION_INSET` (1) in `crates/tui/src/ui/question.rs`, citing this entry. Remove both, and this entry, when `layout.css` names them and the generator carries them.

contradictions.design_says: `tokens/colors.css`: `--label3` is the “tertiary: line numbers, folders, pending” tone — 2.5:1 on `--win` in the dark theme, 2.9:1 in the light — and the caption over the review frames G–J: “⌃↩ stays grey until every file is read, then turns blue.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Apple's HIG (Accessibility): “Strive to meet color contrast minimum standards.” — 4.5:1 for text up to 17 pts — and “Convey information with more than color alone.”
contradictions.app_follows: The design's `label3`, unchanged (the developer's decision, 2026-09-24). The not-ready approve does not rely on colour alone: until every file is read its words say so too, and they change when it is ready.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `D`: under the running `● Check that it works` step of the plan in the conversation, `Running the tests. About ten seconds.` in `label2` on the very next row — `<div style="white-space:pre;padding:0 5ch;color:var(--label2)">`, a note belonging to the step.
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame `P plan card`: the note is the card's — `Adding the limiter to build_stack` in `label2`, the name in `--code`, under the running step of the plan docked above the field; `PlanStep`, the component for a step in the conversation, carries a glyph and one line of text.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's call of 2026-09-30, reversing that of 2026-09-27: a step's note is frame P's, given by the `plan` tool and drawn only in the card. The plan in the conversation (frames B and D) has no note; what the agent says about the running step there is its own prose, and the `stopping` scene draws that sentence as prose.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `J` draws `›` at the end of the `✓ Saved 3 files` row, and the README calls the saved review “one line you can open again”.
contradictions.design_also_says: ADR 0009 §4: nothing is written before an approve, and the approve writes the changeset whole; after it, the files on disk and git's history are the record of what landed.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's decision of 2026-09-27: a saved review is not reopened. The changeset is dropped at the write, and the row is drawn without the `›`.

contradictions.design_says: README: “Comments ride at the end of their line, `◆ Use config`, like an Xcode annotation. The code is never broken up.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Apple's HIG (Layout): “For example, horizontally adjacent views may need to stack vertically to provide more space for text; table rows or other containers may need to grow in height so that text isn’t cropped or doesn’t overlap other content; and table rows with a single line of text by default might need to grow vertically to accommodate multiple lines of text.”
contradictions.app_follows: The HIG (the developer's decision, 2026-09-24): a diff line longer than the pane wraps onto continuation rows with a blank gutter, rather than being cut at the pane's edge. The same holds for a comment with no room beside its line (the developer's decision, 2026-09-29): it takes a row of its own under the line, with a blank gutter, rather than being cut to nothing.

contradictions.design_says: The design system's components are Frame, Field, StatusBar, ContextBar, UserEcho, Prose, Disclosure, PlanStep, Mark, LaunchCard, QuestionPanel, CommandRow and the review set; none of them connects an account, and no frame shows a code to enter elsewhere.
contradictions.design_also_says: The Content Fundamentals: lead with a sentence, outcomes not tool names. A device-code sign-in is one URL, one code and one outcome.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0012 — bare `/connect` is a QuestionPanel listing the accounts ("Which account?", each with the subscription it needs as its fact); the sign-in's prompt ("Open <url> and enter the code <code>. It is good for 30 minutes.") and its outcome ("Connected to x.ai. …") are notices. Retired when the design system draws a connection of its own.

contradictions.design_says: No frame and no component draws the model's reasoning; the working line says only `Thinking` while it runs.
contradictions.design_also_says: The Content Fundamentals: "Technical detail sits one disclosure below, exact and unabridged", drawn as the `Disclosure` component that Space opens.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0015 and 0018 — a turn's thoughts join its one work `Disclosure`, the summary leading with `Thinking` while one streams, then the time added up (`Thought for 6s · Read 3 files`); opened, each thought is a `DetailRow` (`Thought`, its time right-flush) with the reasoning unabridged under it on the prose column in `label2`. Retired when the design system draws reasoning of its own.

contradictions.design_says: The glyph table is closed: `guidelines/glyphs.html` and every character a frame draws inside a window. Since the working line replaced `Working…` (2026-09-29 re-sync), no frame draws `…`.
contradictions.design_also_says: README, Content fundamentals: “Sentence case for prose, labels and keys: *Ready*, *Working…*, *Stop* …” — the design still spells a label with `…`, and gives nothing else to mark text cut short to fit.
contradictions.app_follows: `…` where text is shortened to fit its row (`grid::elide`, `grid::truncate_spans`, `log::first_line`, the working line's phrase) and as a running call's fact before it has one. Retired when the glyph table lists it or a frame draws a shortened row.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `W1` and its section: “In the mark column, the running ● blinks to ○ and back every half second … The context bar drops its label and … its ten segments grow from the thin ━ to the full █ block”; every footer opens with a state glyph and names keys as glyph, a space, verb (`↑↓ Choose`).
contradictions.design_also_says: README: “The caret blinks at 1.05s, stepped. Nothing else animates.”, “Ten `━` segments” and “Glyph, two spaces, verb”; `StatusBar.jsx` draws the mark column empty unless running and `ContextBar.jsx` prints `Context` before ten `━`.
contradictions.app_follows: The frame, as it did over `⎋` on 2026-09-25 (docs/design/IMPORT.md, “Re-sync — 2026-09-29, the working line”): the working line animates, the bar is ten `GAUGE_CELL`s with no label, and a key hint has one space. Retired when the README and the two components are brought up to the frame.

contradictions.design_says: The frame's working section: “There is no key hint: esc always stops, and the launch card says so once.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame `A launch` draws the card as the mark beside four facts — `Aldwin` and its version, `Project`, `Branch`, `Model` — and names no key.
contradictions.app_follows: Frame A: the card names no key, and the working line names none either. `esc` stops a turn as it does in every terminal app (HIG, “Keyboards”: familiar keys). Retired when a frame draws the card's line about `esc`.

contradictions.design_says: The frame draws paths, commands and names in `var(--code)`, which its script sets: `setProperty('--code', this.light() ? 'oklch(0.5 0.1 218)' : 'oklch(0.8 0.085 212)')`.
contradictions.design_also_says: README: “Every token value here is copied from that page”; `tokens/colors.css` declares no `--code`, and the README's colour section names no code ink.
contradictions.app_follows: The frame: the generator reads `--code` from its script into `Palette::code` (`crates/review/src/tokens.rs`, `frame_roles`). Retired when `tokens/colors.css` declares `--code`, which the generator then prefers.

contradictions.design_says: The conversation section: “While working it says what Aldwin is doing and how long it has been at it; esc always stops, so no key is named.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame `K queued` draws messages sent while Aldwin works as one band marked `Queued`, and names no way to take one back before it goes.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's call of 2026-09-29: while messages are queued, `esc` moves them back into the field, ahead of anything typed there, and the next `esc` stops the turn; a stopped or failed turn puts the queue back too, so nothing is sent without the developer. Still no key is named. Retired when the design says what `esc` does with a queue.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `P plan card`: the turn's work row is `✓ Read 3 files … ›` — a `label3` `✓` in the mark column, the summary in `label2`, and the `›` flush right with an empty mark column after it.
contradictions.design_also_says: Frames `B`, `C` and `E` draw the same row as `Read 3 files  ›`: nothing in the mark column and the `›` two spaces after the summary, the row ADR 0018 records.
contradictions.app_follows: Frames B, C and E and ADR 0018 (the developer's call, 2026-09-30: frame P's row is not part of the plan card). Retired when the frames draw one row.

contradictions.design_says: README: “Green and red appear only in diffs.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame `P plan card`: each step's file carries its staged line counts on the card in the conversation — `limit.rs  +48` and `router.rs  +6 −1`, the `+` counts in `--add` and the `−` in `--del`.
contradictions.app_follows: Frame P, as the developer adopted it on 2026-09-30: a staged file's counts are its diff's, in the diff's colours; nothing else outside the review is green or red. `the_agents_prose_is_never_blue_and_nothing_outside_a_diff_is_red` leaves the `drafting` scene out for this. Retired when the README names the counts.

contradictions.design_says: Frames `G` and `P plan card` title the changes with a summary the frame writes: `Rate limiting for the gateway`, in weight 600 over the review and in `label` on the plan card.
contradictions.design_also_says: The product has nothing to write that summary from: no tool gives the changes a title, and the design says nothing of where it comes from.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's request, its first line without a trailing `.` or `!`, as the review's title and the plan card's (`App::changes_title`), `Changes` when nothing was typed. Retired when the design says where the title comes from, or a tool gives one.
